unit.title: Idioms, expressions & register
unit.subtitle: Sound native: everyday idioms and knowing when to be formal

grammar.title: Say it the way Spaniards actually say it
grammar.intro: At B2 the grammar is mostly in place — now you polish the colour. Two things separate a textbook speaker from a natural one: idioms (fixed expressions you can't translate word for word) and register (choosing formal or informal for the situation). Learn the meaning of each idiom as a whole, and match your tone to the person.

sections.heading: Idioms: learn the meaning, not the words
sections.body: These expressions have a fixed meaning that has nothing to do with the literal words. Memorise them as chunks:
conj: to put one's foot in it

ex.en: I don't mind where we eat.

ex.note: vale la pena, not 'vale el dolor'

sections.heading: Feelings & nudges
sections.body: A few more you'll hear constantly — some are reflexive, so the verb changes with the person:

ex.en: Get moving, we're going to be late!
ex.note: ponerse las pilas = shake it up

sections.heading: Register: formal vs informal
sections.body: Choose usted and softened requests with people you don't know or must respect; use tú and direct requests with friends. Compare the same request:

ex.en: Do you mind opening the window? (friend)
Would you be so kind as to sign here?

takeaways: Idioms are chunks: echar de menos = to miss, dar igual = to not matter, valer la pena = to be worth it.
tener ganas de + infinitive = to feel like; estar harto de = to be fed up with.
ponerse las pilas = get moving; meter la pata = put your foot in it; tomar el pelo = tease.
Informal: tú + ¿Puedes…? / ¿Te importa…? — Formal: usted + ¿Podría…? / ¿Le importaría…? / ¿Sería tan amable de…?
Match your register to the person, and never translate idioms word for word.

mistakes.why: 'To miss someone' is the idiom echar de menos, not the literal perder (to lose).

mistakes.w: Estoy cansado de esperar. (to a stranger, using tú)
mistakes.why: Register mismatch: with someone you don't know, use usted and a softened, polite request.
The fixed expression is valer la pena — 'pena', not a literal translation of 'pain'.

exercises.prompt: Cuando estoy de viaje, ___ a mi familia.
exercises.prompt_en: When I'm travelling, I miss my family.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! echar de menos = to miss someone.
exercises.no: 'To miss someone' is the idiom “echar de menos”, not perder.

exercises.prompt: A stranger at reception: “___ esperar un momento?”
exercises.prompt_en: Would you be so kind as to wait a moment? (formal)
exercises.ok: ¡Exacto! Con desconocidos, registro formal: ¿Sería tan amable de…?
exercises.no: With a stranger, use the formal register: “¿Sería tan amable de esperar…?”

exercises.prompt: Build: “I feel like going to the beach.”
exercises.no: “Tengo ganas de ir a la playa” — tener ganas de + infinitive.

exercises.prompt: Me da ___: puedes elegir tú el restaurante.
exercises.prompt_en: I don't mind: you can choose the restaurant.
exercises.ok: ¡Bien! Me da igual = it's all the same to me.
exercises.no: The idiom is “dar igual”: Me da igual.

exercises.prompt: Match each idiom to its meaning.
pairs: to put one's foot in it

exercises.tts: Estoy harto de esperar el autobús.
accepted: estoy harto de esperar el autobus
exercises.translation: I'm fed up with waiting for the bus.
exercises.no: It was: “Estoy harto de esperar el autobús.” (I'm fed up with waiting for the bus.)

exercises.scenario: Your manager asks you, politely and formally, for a favour 🧑‍💼

lines.speaker: Sra. Díaz
lines.es: ¿Le importaría enviarme el informe antes de las cinco?
lines.en: Would you mind sending me the report before five?

options.text: Claro, se lo envío enseguida. No hay problema.
Qué va, tío, paso de eso ahora mismo.

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! Respondes en un registro cortés que encaja con la pregunta formal.
exercises.no: Match the formal register: “Claro, se lo envío enseguida. No hay problema.” The other replies are too informal or rude.

exercises.say: Vale la pena ponerse las pilas.
exercises.en: It's worth getting your act together.
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the sound.
